claude.interpret: The economic shape is exactly what I want from a tail flag — it gets more right as the horizon lengthens and it doubles the breach rate in the crowded index. That is a usable allocation tell even if the p-value is soft, because I am buying asymmetric protection, not betting the farm on the mean.
claude.act: I am comfortable treating COR1M<8 as a standing 'raise hedge readiness' flag at small size. I will not size it like a high-conviction signal until it survives out-of-sample.

claude.interpret: This is the textbook clustering trap. 36 'observations' are 8 episodes; the moving-block bootstrap p of 0.13/0.23 is the honest number and it does not clear 0.05. The lift figures are real but rest on ~8 independent draws, almost all from 2024-26 — a single regime, not a tested distribution.
claude.act: Verdict must stay weak_support; do not promote to a mechanical trigger. The only thing that moves this is genuine out-of-sample episodes (E-COR-103) and a multiple-testing correction (E-COR-104). I would explicitly forbid threshold tuning.

claude.interpret: From a risk-budget seat, a flag that roughly doubles the odds of a -5% breach and reliably precedes negative drift is actionable as insurance, because the cost of a small hedge is bounded and the payoff is convex. The danger is over-trusting it and over-hedging into the 11 of 12 times it's noise.
claude.act: Implement as a small, rules-light tilt: on COR1M<8 add a modest QQQ-skewed hedge, cap the premium spend, let it expire if no breach. Pair with H-COR-003 to confirm it adds something VIX wasn't already telling me.
